unit.title: Agent engineering: planning, multi-agent, evals and guardrails

lesson.title: Plans and memory
lesson.subtitle: How agents plan, why errors carry forward, and what fits in the window

chapters.label: Choosing what stays, and the lab

scenes.visual: A list: Two steps: fine; I said yes; it said hello; My question fell out.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: My agent did the first two steps perfectly. Then I replied yes, and it greeted me like a stranger! Nothing was broken. My question had just fallen out of its memory.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how agents plan, and what fits in their memory.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Agents plan in two common ways. Plan first: write every step, then run them. Or step by step: look at each result, then choose the next step. Darsi Tiny writes a one-line plan, then calls its tools in turn.

scenes.visual: A list: Timetable: “no school”; Reminder set anyway: “6B: 6B”; Check each result first.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Each step builds on the last. On Saturday, the timetable tool answers: no school. Darsi Tiny sets the reminder anyway: six B, six B. A failed step that nobody checks becomes the next step’s input.

scenes.visual: A list: The tools; The conversation so far; Room to write; Darsi Tiny 384; big models ~128,000.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: An agent’s only memory is its context window: every token the model reads at once. It holds the tools, the conversation so far, and room to write. Darsi Tiny’s holds three hundred and eighty-four tokens; big cloud models, about a hundred and twenty-eight thousand.

scenes.visual: A list: Keep everything: 4th answer cut; Drop the oldest: the question falls out; Keep notes: all 7 work.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: When the window fills, the app chooses what stays. Keep everything, and the fourth answer is cut off. Drop the oldest, and the question behind a yes falls out. Keep short notes, and all seven messages work.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! The app drops the oldest turns. I ask for tomorrow’s weather, it asks which village, and I say Dala. It gives me today’s weather. Why?

scenes.visual: A list: The model never saw it; So it used a default: today; It can’t say what it forgot; Only the app knows.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Because tomorrow fell out of the window. The model never saw it, so it used a default. It can’t tell you what it has forgotten. Only the app knows what it dropped.

scenes.visual: A list: Keep recent turns; Older turns become notes; Pin the key facts; Retrieval: fetch what’s needed.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So engineers decide what stays. Keep recent turns, and turn older ones into notes. Pin the facts the task depends on, like the day and the place. Or fetch from documents only the part a step needs: that’s retrieval.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In this lesson’s code, you’ll write the trimming. Walk back from the newest turn, adding up tokens. Stop at the first turn that won’t fit, so the conversation has no gaps.

scenes.visual: A list: Send 7 messages; Keep everything; Drop the oldest, at 128; Keep notes.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, send seven messages and watch the window fill. Try Keep everything, then Drop the oldest at a hundred and twenty-eight tokens, then Keep notes. See which turn falls out.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. An agent helps plan a three-day field trip over a long chat. Which memory strategy is safest?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Check each result as you go; The window is its only memory; The app decides what stays.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Check each result as you go · The window is its only memory · The app decides what stays
scenes.narration: Notes, with the dates and places pinned. Remember: check each step’s result as you go. The context window is the model’s only memory. And the app, not the model, decides what stays.

scenes.visual: A list: An agent for a week of group study; Pin a two-line note: who, what, when, where; Decide what it may drop.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: picture an agent that helps your group study for a week. Write the two-line note you would pin at the top of its window: who, what, when and where. Then decide what it may drop.

checkpoints.prompt: The app drops the oldest turns. Someone asks for tomorrow’s weather, is asked which village, and says “Dala”. The agent gives today’s weather. Why?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the turn with “tomorrow” was dropped, so the model never saw it and filled in a default. It can’t tell you what it forgot.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — Dala was read fine. The word “tomorrow” was in an older turn that the app dropped, so the model never saw it.

checkpoints.prompt: An agent helps plan a three-day field trip over a long chat. Which memory strategy is safest?

options.text: Keep everything until it’s cut off
Drop the oldest turns as it fills
Keep notes, with the dates and places pinned

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — notes keep what was asked and answered in fewer tokens, and pinning the dates and places means the facts the plan depends on never fall out.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — keeping everything stops when the window is full, and dropping the oldest loses the first days’ details. Notes with pinned facts keep what matters.
